text:
maria: Heads up — we need a concise runbook and consensus on Terraform/Pulumi module layout + remote state/CICD wiring for the new eu-west-3 GPU region. Goal: reproducible bring-up that oncall/infra-PM can follow and hand off.

jon: +1. do we prefer pure terraform or allow pulumi for some pieces? we had trouble with pulumi service auth last time.

ashish: prefer modules that can be used by either runtime but with the same remote-state conventions. keep infra-as-code primitives opinionated: networking, cluster, autoscaling, quotas.

samir: flag: GPU quota requests for eu-west-3 are slow — we should include a quota ticket template and an early step to request quotas before apply.

kelsey: agree. also: cost estimate step required. gpu hourly estimates and ephemeral nodepool sizing.

maria: sketching a proposal: 1) mono-repo with /modules/{network,iam,cluster,gpu-quotas,monitoring} 2) per-region overlays under /envs/eu-west-3 using either terraform workspaces or pulumi stacks 3) remote state: S3 bucket + DynamoDB lock (aws) or GCS + Firestore lock (gcp) based on cloud 4) CICD: GitHub Actions pipeline with plan -> PR -> approval -> apply-runner in bastion account 5) smoke tests post-apply and an automated cost report. sound doable?

jon: sounds good. small suggestion: keep one infra repo per cloud family to reduce blast radius. eu-west-3 is AWS so put it under infra-aws.

ashish: implementation details: terraform state naming convention: <org>-infra-<region>-<component>-state, bucket encryption = AES256 + KMS key, dynamodb table name = <org>-locks. include lifecycle rule for state retention/backups.

samir: quota ticket template (short):
```
Subject: Request GPU quota increase for eu-west-3
Body:
- Project: Redwood Inference - eu-west-3 bring-up
- Instances requested: p4d.24xlarge x4 (estimated), g5.12xlarge x10
- Start date: <date>
- Justification: production inference capacity for customer X, will be isolated in dedicated VPC
- Contact: samir@redwood.com
```

kelsey: CICD gating: require terraform plan artifact in PR comment and `apply` can only run from protected branch with `infra-approvers` required for merge. Also use OPA policy check step (rego) to prevent wide-open security groups.

maria: include the validation checklist in the runbook: 1) VPC and subnets match CIDR plan 2) Route tables & IGW/NAT correct 3) Security groups scoped 4) EKS/Managed cluster control plane reachable 5) GPU instances launch and nvidia drivers bootstrap 6) Node autoscaler observes pods 7) Prometheus metrics and alerting rules firing 8) Cross-region S3 replication config for snapshots if needed.

jon: for driver bootstrap include DaemonSet with `nvidia/cuda` image and a short job `kubectl -n kube-system run gpu-check --rm --restart=Never --image=alpine -- nvidia-smi`. also check `kubectl get nodes -o wide` for LABELS `gpu=true`.

ashish: Pulumi notes: if teams want pulumi, require pulumi backend to be the same S3 bucket (pulumi login s3://<bucket>) or pulumi service with org project pinned. However prefer pulumi only for higher-level orchestration, not for low-level networking modules to avoid drift.

infra-bot: Reminder: create AWS KMS key for state encryption before terraform apply, assign key policy to CI role and infra admins.

samir: CI runner details: use a self-hosted runner in a management account with an assumed-role pattern into target region accounts. avoid long-lived creds in GH secrets; use OIDC where possible.

kelsey: sample GitHub Actions job (plan):
```
name: infra-plan
on: [pull_request]
jobs:
  plan:
    runs-on: self-hosted-infra
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@v3
      - name: setup terraform
        uses: hashicorp/setup-terraform@v2
      - name: terraform init
        run: terraform init -backend-config=\"bucket=${{ secrets.TF_STATE_BUCKET }}\" -backend-config=\"key=eu-west-3/network.tfstate\"
      - name: terraform plan
        run: terraform plan -out=tfplan
      - name: upload plan
        run: gh actions upload-artifact --name tfplan --path tfplan
```

maria: for apply we want a runner that assumes a short-lived role and requires manual approval via PR merge and an `apply` workflow triggered only on `push` to `infra/main`. Documented step: run `terraform apply -input=false tfplan` with lock table present.

jon: who owns post-apply smoke tests? ops-oncall? propose a step in CICD to run smoke tests and only mark PR as complete if smoke tests pass, else auto-create an incident draft.

ashish: smoke tests we should automate: 
- curl /health on internal control-plane endpoints
- kubectl get nodes count matches expected
- run gpu-check job and assert exit 0
- check CloudWatch/Stackdriver that /var/log/cloud-init has no errors

samir: handoff checklist for oncall/infra-PM: 
- Link to module docs + variable reference
- Terraform/Pulumi backend config snippet
- Contact list for cloud support + account ids
- Quota tickets created and approved
- Cost dashboard link + expected burn rate
- How to scale nodepools and emergency rollback steps
- Post-mortem template in case of issues during bring-up

maria: adding a short example backend snippet (AWS Terraform):
```
terraform {
  backend "s3" {
    bucket = \"redwood-infra-state-eu-west-3\"
    key    = \"network/terraform.tfstate\"
    region = \"eu-west-3\"
    dynamodb_table = \"redwood-infra-locks\"
    encrypt = true
  }
}
```

kelsey: include a `validate` make target in repo: `make validate` runs `terraform fmt -check`, `terraform validate`, `rego` policies, and `tflint`. add `make smoke` to run the smoke scripts against the cluster endpoints.

jon: security note: ensure IAM roles for the node IAM profile are limited (no full-admin). Use IAM policies scoped to ekc:Create/Describe only. attach a policy review step in PR.

maria: final operational runbook summary I propose we add to docs (short):
- Preflight (quota, KMS, bucket, CI runner)
- Plan (open PR, run plan)
- Approve (infra approvers + security + cost)
- Apply (protected workflow, assume role, lock)
- Validate (smoke tests, kube checks, driver checks)
- Handoff (Slack ping #oncall, create runbook task, share cost dashboard)

ashish: ACK. I'll draft the detailed repo README + templates and push a PR to infra-aws/eu-west-3 by EOD tomorrow.

samir: i'll prepare quota ticket drafts and contact cloud support.

kelsey: i'll add GH Actions templates and OPA policies to the repo.

maria: great — once PR lands i'll run through the runbook with @oncall and mark the handoff doc ready. leaving a sticky note: include rollback playbook for nodepool scaling and how to detach GPU nodepools from autoscaler. :white_check_mark:
